plant.description: Pineapple (Ananas comosus) is not on the ASPCA toxic-plant list, and ripe flesh is non-toxic to cats in very small amounts. The hazard comes from unripe fruit and the plant's fibrous parts, which are high in bromelain — a proteolytic (protein-digesting) enzyme that causes oral irritation and mild-to-moderate gastrointestinal upset rather than systemic poisoning. A pineapple is a tropical plant with a large, edible multiple fruit consisting of coalesced berries. An unripened pineapple is one that has been harvested or encountered before reaching full maturity. In this raw form, the fruit is typically hard, green, exceptionally acidic, and not yet sweet. It is most commonly encountered as a whole fresh fruit.

toxins.name: Bromelain
toxins.description: Bromelain is a proteolytic (protein-digesting) enzyme present in high concentration in unripe pineapple and the plant's fibrous parts. It is not a systemic poison; instead it causes local irritation by breaking down protein in the mucous membranes of the mouth and digestive tract, leading to oral irritation/pain and mild-to-moderate gastrointestinal upset. Tough, fibrous plant parts (skin, core, leaves) can also act as a mechanical/choking hazard and cause digestive upset from insoluble fibre.

symptoms.name: Oral pain and mouth irritation
symptoms.notes: Bromelain, a proteolytic enzyme, irritates the mucous membranes of the mouth; spiny rind and leaves can add mechanical irritation.

symptoms.name: Drooling (hypersalivation)
symptoms.notes: Hypersalivation typically accompanies oral irritation from bromelain and fibrous plant parts.

symptoms.name: Vomiting
symptoms.notes: Mild-to-moderate, self-limiting gastrointestinal upset from bromelain and high fibre/sugar content.

symptoms.name: Diarrhea
symptoms.notes: Mild-to-moderate, self-limiting gastrointestinal upset from high insoluble fibre and sugar.

treatments.name: Based on the provided sources, there is no specific, isolated treatment protocol detailed exclusively for unripened pineapples. However
Rinse the Mouth and Offer Water
treatments.description: Gently rinsing the mouth and offering fresh water can help wash away residual bromelain and ease oral irritation.
treatments.notes: Oral irritation from bromelain and fibrous plant parts is usually mild and self-limiting; rinsing helps relieve discomfort.

treatments.name: Monitor and Provide Supportive Care for GI Upset
treatments.description: Watch for vomiting, diarrhea, drooling, or oral discomfort and keep the cat hydrated; contact a veterinarian if signs persist or the cat ate a large amount.
treatments.notes: Effects are typically mild-to-moderate, self-limiting gastrointestinal upset; veterinary supportive care (such as fluids) may be warranted if symptoms persist or the cat becomes dehydrated.
